title: C library
summary: C programs compiled against Breenix's own clean-room C library behave as ISO C17 and POSIX.1-2024 specify across stdio, string and stdlib, math, locale and wide characters, directories and globbing, getopt and the environment, and threads, and BusyBox built on that library runs its applets.

cases.title: fopen of a missing file in mode r returns NULL with errno ENOENT
fopen mode w truncates an existing file to length 0
fopen mode a writes at the end of file even after fseek to the start
fopen mode r+ updates in place without truncating, with fseek between read and write
fopen mode wx fails with EEXIST on an existing file and creates a new one
fopen creates a file with mode 0666 less the umask (0644 under umask 022)
A fully buffered stream (_IOFBF) holds output until fflush
A line-buffered stream (_IOLBF) writes when a newline is written
An unbuffered stream (_IONBF) writes each byte at once
fflush(NULL) flushes every output stream
fseek with SEEK_SET, SEEK_END and SEEK_CUR moves the position ftell reports, and rewind resets it
fseek to a negative offset fails with EINVAL and leaves the position unchanged
ungetc pushes back a byte the next read returns without changing the file, and ungetc(EOF) fails
ungetc clears the end-of-file indicator
printf %d %i %u %o %x %X and the # flag format integers, and the return is the length
printf field widths, precisions and the - 0 + space flags pad integers as C17 7.21.6.1 specifies
printf %c, %s with precision and width, and %% format as specified
printf %f %e %g %G with precisions and the # flag, rounding 2.5 to even under %.0f
printf length modifiers l ll h hh z j t convert their arguments to the named type
printf writes inf/infinity and nan for infinities and NaNs, honouring the field width
snprintf truncates to the buffer size, always terminates, and returns the untruncated length
sscanf %d %x %o %i read decimal, hexadecimal, octal and prefixed integers
sscanf field widths and %[ scansets, including negated sets, stop where specified
sscanf %lf and %f read exponents, signs and inf
sscanf returns EOF on empty input, 0 on a mismatch, and does not count suppressed or %n conversions
fgets stops after a newline or at size-1 bytes and returns NULL at end of file
getline grows the buffer for a 301-byte line, reads an unterminated last line and returns -1 at end of file
freopen redirects stdout to a file that later output reaches
tmpfile returns a stream open for update that reads back what was written
A failed write sets the error indicator, not end-of-file, and clearerr clears it
The end-of-file indicator is set only once a read goes past the end, and clearerr clears it
open_memstream grows a buffer and updates its pointer and size on fflush
exit flushes buffered output streams before the process ends
perror writes the prefix, a colon and space, strerror(errno) and a newline to stderr
fclose flushes buffered output and closes the underlying descriptor
memcpy copies and memmove handles overlap in both directions, each returning the destination
memset and memchr convert their byte to unsigned char, and memchr searches past NUL only within n
memcmp compares bytes as unsigned char and only within n
strlen and strnlen return the length, strnlen at most maxlen
strncpy pads with NUL to n and writes no terminator for a longer source, and stpcpy returns the end
strcat appends, and strncat appends at most n bytes and always a terminator
strcmp and strncmp compare as unsigned char, and strcasecmp/strncasecmp ignore case
strchr and strrchr find the first and last byte, including the terminator
strstr finds a needle after a partial match, returns the haystack for an empty needle and NULL when absent
strspn, strcspn and strpbrk measure and find spans of accepted and rejected bytes
strtok and strtok_r skip runs of delimiters and return NULL after the last token
strdup and strndup return new copies, strndup at most n bytes
strerror gives text per error, and strerror_r into a too-small buffer returns ERANGE
In the C locale strcoll orders by byte value and strxfrm preserves that order
strtol reads bases 0, 16 and 36, signs and leading space, and sets the end pointer
strtol and strtoll return LONG_MAX, LONG_MIN or LLONG_MAX with ERANGE on overflow, consuming every digit
strtol with no digits returns 0 with the end pointer at the start, "0x" without a hex digit reads 0, and base 1 fails with EINVAL
strtoul negates "-1" to ULONG_MAX without error, and strtoull overflow gives ULLONG_MAX with ERANGE
strtod reads decimal, hexadecimal, infinity, nan(...) and negative zero, setting the end pointer
strtod overflow returns HUGE_VAL with ERANGE and underflow at most DBL_MIN with ERANGE
atoi, atol, atoll and atof convert leading numbers
qsort sorts 1000 integers into order without losing any, and accepts zero elements
qsort moves whole 24-byte records, and bsearch finds present keys and returns NULL for absent ones
malloc returns memory aligned for max_align_t, and free(NULL) does nothing
malloc of SIZE_MAX or SIZE_MAX/2 returns NULL with errno ENOMEM
calloc returns zeroed memory, and NULL with ENOMEM when nmemb*size overflows
realloc(NULL) allocates, and growing or shrinking keeps the contents
A realloc that fails returns NULL with ENOMEM and leaves the old block intact
posix_memalign and aligned_alloc align as asked, and a non-power-of-two alignment returns EINVAL
atexit handlers run in reverse order of registration when exit is called
setenv honours overwrite, unsetenv removes, and names that are empty or contain = fail with EINVAL
div and ldiv truncate toward zero, and abs, labs and llabs return magnitudes
rand returns values in 0..RAND_MAX and repeats its sequence after the same srand seed
sqrt is correctly rounded, keeps -0 and returns inf for inf
sqrt(-1) returns NaN with a domain error: EDOM and FE_INVALID as math_errhandling says
math_errhandling is MATH_ERRNO|MATH_ERREXCEPT (Linux policy)
log and log10 of zero are pole errors (-HUGE_VAL, ERANGE, FE_DIVBYZERO) and log(-1) a domain error
exp(1000) overflows to HUGE_VAL with ERANGE and FE_OVERFLOW, and exp(-1000) underflows to +0
pow returns 1 for a zero exponent or base 1 even with NaN, and exact results for the IEC 60559 special cases
pow of a negative base to a non-integer is a domain error, of zero to a negative power a pole error, and overflow a range error
fmod takes the sign of the dividend, returns x for an infinite divisor and keeps -0
fmod of an infinite dividend or a zero divisor returns NaN with a domain error
remainder rounds the quotient to even, and remquo returns its sign and low bits
frexp splits into a fraction in [0.5, 1) and an exponent, including -0 and the smallest subnormal
ldexp scales by powers of two into the subnormal range and overflows with ERANGE and FE_OVERFLOW
modf splits into fraction and integral parts with the argument's sign, including infinities
round, ceil, floor and trunc round as specified and keep the sign of zero results
rint and nearbyint round in the current rounding direction set by fesetround
fegetround starts at FE_TONEAREST, reports what fesetround set, an invalid mode fails, and arithmetic follows the mode
lround rounds halves away from zero, lrint to even, and an out-of-range lround raises FE_INVALID
Division by zero, invalid operations and overflow raise their flags, and feraiseexcept and feclearexcept set and clear them
feholdexcept clears and saves the flags, feupdateenv merges them back, and fegetexceptflag/fesetexceptflag restore one
fpclassify and isnan, isinf, isfinite and isnormal classify NaN, infinity, subnormal, zero and normal values
nan("") is a NaN unequal to itself, and the quiet comparison macros return false without FE_INVALID
copysign and fabs set and clear the sign, and signbit reads it from zeros and NaNs
hypot is exact for 3,4, returns inf for inf and NaN, and does not overflow for 1e300,1e300
sin, tan and atan2 keep the signs of zeros, and atan2 and atan return the IEC 60559 multiples of pi
sin, cos, asin, acos and tanh are within an ulp, including sin(1e22) with full argument reduction
sin and cos of infinity and acos/asin outside [-1, 1] return NaN with a domain error
exp(0) and log(1) are exact, exp2 is exact for integers, and log2, log10, log and cbrt are within an ulp
log1p and expm1 keep -0 and tiny arguments, log1p(-1) is a pole error and log1p(-2) a domain error
The float functions sqrtf, floorf, fmodf, ldexpf and expf compute in float, expf overflowing with ERANGE
tgamma and lgamma give known values, tgamma(+0) is a pole error and tgamma(-1) a domain error
erf and erfc give their limits at zero and infinity and erf(1) within an ulp
fma computes x*y+z with one rounding
fmax and fmin ignore a NaN argument, and fdim returns the positive difference or +0
nextafter steps one ulp, from zero to the smallest subnormal, and overflows from DBL_MAX with ERANGE
ilogb, logb, scalbn and scalbln give exponents and scale, logb(0) raises FE_DIVBYZERO and ilogb(0) FE_INVALID
A program starts in the C locale, which has MB_CUR_MAX 1
setlocale accepts POSIX and C, and selecting POSIX reports C or POSIX
setlocale of an unknown locale returns NULL and leaves the locale unchanged
setlocale(LC_ALL, "") with no locale variables selects C, and LC_ALL overrides LC_CTYPE
localeconv in the C locale returns the values C17 7.11.2.1 gives
nl_langinfo(CODESET) is UTF-8 in C.UTF-8 and RADIXCHAR is . in C
In C.UTF-8 mbrtowc decodes 1-, 2-, 3- and 4-byte characters and returns 0 for NUL
mbrtowc returns (size_t)-2 for an incomplete character and completes it on the next call
mbrtowc rejects a stray byte, an overlong form and a surrogate with EILSEQ
UTF-8 ends at U+10FFFF (RFC 3629, ISO/IEC 10646): mbrtowc and wcrtomb fail with EILSEQ above it and for surrogates
wcrtomb encodes U+20AC and U+10FFFF as UTF-8, and wcrtomb(NULL) returns 1
In the C locale wcrtomb encodes ASCII and fails with EILSEQ for U+20AC
mbstowcs and wcstombs convert a string both ways and report EILSEQ for invalid input
mbsrtowcs advances the source pointer and sets it to NULL at the terminator
mblen and mbtowc report character lengths, and 0 for a stateless encoding's state query
btowc and wctob map single-byte characters and return WEOF or EOF otherwise
wcslen, wcscmp, wcsncmp, wcscpy, wcscat, wcschr, wcsrchr, wcsstr and wcsspn work on wide strings
wmemcpy, wmemmove, wmemset, wmemchr and wmemcmp work on wide-character arrays
wcstol and wcstod read wide strings, set the end pointer and report ERANGE
In C.UTF-8 iswalpha, iswupper, iswlower, towupper and towlower handle Latin and Greek, and iswdigit only 0-9
In the C locale the wctype functions classify ASCII only, and towupper(WEOF) is WEOF
wctype, iswctype, wctrans and towctrans look up classes and mappings by name, and 0 for unknown names
A stream starts unoriented, the first wide or byte operation orients it, and fwide cannot change that
fputws writes UTF-8 bytes in C.UTF-8 and fgetws reads them back
fgetwc of an invalid byte returns WEOF with EILSEQ and sets the error indicator
swprintf formats %d %ls %lc, fails when the result does not fit, and snprintf %ls converts to UTF-8
newlocale and uselocale give the thread C.UTF-8, and uselocale(LC_GLOBAL_LOCALE) restores the global C locale
opendir fails with ENOENT for a missing path and ENOTDIR for a file
readdir returns ., .. and every entry exactly once, then NULL without changing errno
readdir gives d_ino equal to stat's st_ino and d_type DT_REG and DT_DIR (Linux ABI)
readdir of an empty directory returns only . and ..
readdir returns each of 300 entries exactly once
rewinddir rescans and sees an entry created after opendir
seekdir to a telldir position makes readdir return the same entry again
dirfd returns the stream's directory descriptor, and fdopendir reads a directory descriptor and fails with ENOTDIR for a file
scandir applies its filter and sorts with alphasort
glob("*.c") returns the sorted matches and a NULL-terminated gl_pathv
glob ? and [ ] bracket expressions, including [!...], match single characters
glob with no match returns GLOB_NOMATCH, and GLOB_NOCHECK returns the pattern
glob * does not match a leading period, and a pattern starting with . does
GLOB_MARK appends / to directories only
GLOB_DOOFFS reserves NULL slots and GLOB_APPEND adds a second pattern's matches
glob matches patterns in several path components
A backslash in a glob pattern quotes the next character, unless GLOB_NOESCAPE
fnmatch * and ? match strings, returning 0 or FNM_NOMATCH
With FNM_PATHNAME a slash is matched only by a slash, not by *, ? or a bracket expression
With FNM_PERIOD a leading period, also after a slash with FNM_PATHNAME, is matched only explicitly
A backslash in fnmatch quotes the next character, unless FNM_NOESCAPE
fnmatch bracket expressions: ranges, negation, ] and - as members, and character classes
FNM_CASEFOLD matches without regard to case
optind starts at 1 and opterr at 1
getopt returns each option, then -1 at the first operand with optind pointing at it
getopt takes an option-argument attached to its option
getopt takes an option-argument from the next argument
getopt returns grouped options one by one and advances optind after the group
getopt takes the rest of a group as an option-argument
getopt returns -1 at -- and steps optind past it
getopt returns -1 at the first operand and does not permute argv (POSIX)
getopt treats - as an operand
getopt returns ? and sets optopt for an unknown option, printing nothing when opterr is 0
getopt writes a diagnostic naming an unknown option to stderr when opterr is set
getopt returns ? and sets optopt when an option-argument is missing
getopt returns : with no diagnostic for a missing option-argument when optstring starts with :
getopt takes an option-argument that starts with -
getopt_long returns the val of a long option without an argument
getopt_long takes a required argument after = or as the next argument
getopt_long stores val in *flag and returns 0 for an option with a flag
getopt_long sets *longindex to the matched option's index
getopt_long accepts a unique prefix of a long option
getopt_long returns ? for an ambiguous prefix
getopt_long gives an optional argument only after =, else optarg NULL
getopt_long returns ? for an unknown long option
getopt_long returns : for a missing required argument when optstring starts with :
getopt_long handles short and long options together
getsubopt returns token indexes and values, and -1 with the whole token for an unknown one
environ at startup is main's envp and holds exactly the environment execve passed
getenv matches whole names only and returns NULL for missing ones
putenv makes the caller's string part of the environment, so changing it changes getenv's result
putenv of an existing name replaces it, leaving one entry
setenv and unsetenv update environ, unsetenv of a missing name succeeds, and empty or = names fail with EINVAL
A child created by fork sees variables set with setenv
pthread_join returns the value the thread's start routine returned
Linux policy: pthread_join of the calling thread fails with EDEADLK
pthread_detach succeeds and the detached thread runs
Threads are joinable by default, an invalid detach state is EINVAL, and a thread created detached runs
pthread_join returns the value given to pthread_exit from a nested call
pthread_self in a thread equals the ID pthread_create returned, and differs from its creator's
Sixteen threads created at once all run and are joined
pthread_mutex_trylock of a locked mutex returns EBUSY, even for the owner, and succeeds once unlocked
An error-checking mutex reports EDEADLK on relock and EPERM on unlock by a non-owner or when unlocked
A recursive mutex is released after as many unlocks as locks, then reports EPERM
Four threads adding 20000 each under a mutex lose no updates
pthread_mutex_timedlock of a held mutex returns ETIMEDOUT, not before its deadline
The default mutex type is PTHREAD_MUTEX_DEFAULT, settype reports EINVAL for an invalid type, and gettype reports what settype set
A robust mutex whose owner exited returns EOWNERDEAD, and pthread_mutex_consistent recovers it
pthread_cond_signal wakes a waiter that sees the predicate set
pthread_cond_broadcast wakes all four waiters
pthread_cond_timedwait returns ETIMEDOUT not before its deadline, with the mutex held again
A condition variable set to CLOCK_MONOTONIC times its wait on that clock; the default clock is CLOCK_REALTIME
pthread_cond_timedwait with a deadline already past returns ETIMEDOUT at once
A read-locked rwlock admits another reader and refuses a writer with EBUSY
A write-locked rwlock refuses readers and writers with EBUSY, and a timed read lock times out
Linux policy: relocking an rwlock the caller holds for writing fails with EDEADLK
pthread_once runs its routine once and returns in every thread only after it finished
Thread-specific data is per thread and its destructor runs at thread exit with each thread's value
A cancelled thread ends at pthread_testcancel and joins as PTHREAD_CANCELED
read is a cancellation point: a thread blocked in read is cancelled
A cancel sent while cancellation is disabled stays pending and acts once enabled
Cleanup handlers pushed with pthread_cleanup_push run when the thread is cancelled
A cancel that arrives as read completes keeps the byte read: the cancelled thread's count and the pipe's remainder add up
A cancel sent while cancellation is disabled does not make nanosleep or a blocking read fail with EINTR
A thread cancelled while blocked in stdio output leaves the stream unlocked, and fclose and fopen still work
A waiter cancelled in pthread_cond_wait does not consume a concurrent pthread_cond_signal another thread waits for
A program exec'd by a thread with cancellation disabled and a cancel request pending starts and runs
pthread_barrier_wait releases all four threads together and gives exactly one PTHREAD_BARRIER_SERIAL_THREAD
pthread_spin_trylock of a held spin lock returns EBUSY and succeeds once unlocked
pthread_attr_setstacksize refuses less than PTHREAD_STACK_MIN and a thread runs on the size set
errno is per thread
pthread_sigmask changes only the calling thread's signal mask
sched_setaffinity narrows and restores the CPU_* set sched_getaffinity reports, with ESRCH for a negative pid and EINVAL for a short or empty set
sh expands $((6*7)) to 42
sh runs printf piped into sort
sh reports $? of false as 1 and exits with the status given to exit
sh runs a for loop with an if and test inside
sh redirects with >, >> and <
echo prints its arguments separated by spaces with a newline
cat concatenates files and - for standard input
ls lists a directory's names sorted, one per line when not on a terminal
ls -l shows a file's mode, size and name
cp copies a file's contents
mv renames a file
rm removes a file and exits 1 for a missing one
mkdir -p creates a nested path
sed s/// substitutes and sed -n 2p prints one line
awk sums a field across lines in an END block
awk printf formats %05.1f, %-3s and %x
grep prints the matching lines and exits 0
grep -E -c counts matches, and grep exits 1 when nothing matches
sort -n orders numerically and sort -r -u reverses and drops duplicates
uniq -c counts adjacent repeated lines
wc -l -w -c counts lines, words and bytes
head -n 2 prints the first two lines
tail -n 1 prints the last line
cut -d: -f2 selects a field
tr a-z A-Z translates a range
find . -name '*.txt' finds files in subdirectories
tar creates an archive, extracts it and lists it
xargs passes standard input as arguments to echo
printf formats %s, %d and %5.2f
expr evaluates 6 * 7
test 1 -lt 2 exits 0 and test 2 -lt 1 exits 1
md5sum of "abc" on standard input is 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72
basename strips the directory and a suffix
dirname strips the last component
date -u -d @0 formats the epoch as 1970-01-01 00:00:00
